seoTitle: Custom Logo Perfume: Private Label Guide | TopPerfume
description: Plan a custom logo perfume order: compare branding options, prepare your artwork, confirm MOQ and samples, and send a clear brief for a private label quote.
excerpt: Learn what to confirm before adding your logo to a fragrance product, from eligible packaging and artwork to quantity, sampling and a written quotation.
title: Custom Logo Perfume: A Private Label Buying Guide
html:
A perfume with your logo starts with a few practical decisions: which product you want to sell, where your branding should appear, and what needs to be approved before production. Getting those decisions clear makes the first quotation more useful—and gives you a better basis for comparing options.

This guide is for retailers and new beauty brands planning a fragrance project. It explains how to prepare a brief, separate different types of customization, and move from an idea to a sample and quotation.

Choose the buying route that matches your plan

Begin by deciding whether you want to purchase finished products for resale or develop a product under your own brand. The available products, minimum quantities and approval steps can differ.

Buying route What you are asking for What to confirm first
Finished-product wholesale An existing product for your retail assortment Exact product reference, quantity, packaging and current availability
Your logo on an eligible product Your brand identity applied through an agreed branding route Product eligibility, logo position, available method and minimum quantity
A wider development project Changes to packaging, fragrance direction or other product details Feasible scope, samples, separate costs and project timing

TopPerfume works as a trading and sourcing partner, reviewing custom projects with suppliers individually. Our low-MOQ perfume and private-label page sets out the current routes. Its starting quantities apply to eligible options; the final scope is confirmed against your brief.

If you are browsing finished products carrying an existing brand, ask us to identify an appropriate private-label option for your project. Buying a branded wholesale product and commissioning your own branded product are separate requests.

Decide where your logo should appear

Think about how a customer will see and handle the product. The bottle is one part of the presentation; the carton, label and other agreed packaging elements may also carry your brand information.

Prepare a simple placement list. For each part, identify what you want to show: the brand name, product name, design element or other approved text. Ask which branding methods are available for the selected component before fixing the artwork.

Questions worth resolving early include:

  • Is the proposed logo position suitable for this bottle or packaging surface?
  • What usable area and artwork dimensions should the designer work to?
  • Which colours and finishes are available for this specific option?
  • Will the quotation cover the bottle branding, outer box or both?
  • What additional product information must be accommodated in the final artwork for the intended market?

Treat a reference image as a way to explain your preferred direction. The agreed specification and approved sample should identify what will actually be supplied.

Prepare the product brief before polishing the design

A useful first message describes the business and product decisions as well as the logo. You can begin while some choices are still open: mark them as questions so the quotation addresses them directly.

Brief field What to include
Business and customers Your shop or brand, target customers and sales channel
Product direction Perfume, fragrance mist or another requested format; preferred size
Fragrance direction Your description of the scent you want to explore, if relevant
Branding scope Bottle, label, carton or other requested elements
Quantity Estimated units, with a breakdown by product or version
Artwork status Logo available, artwork in progress, or guidance requested
Destination Country and city for the shipping discussion
Timing Your preferred launch date and any fixed deadline
Budget A purchasing budget or target cost, if you have one

For example, “one fragrance product with our logo on the bottle and carton” is a clearer starting scope than “fully custom perfume.” It allows the supplier to explain what is available and which decisions still affect the quotation.

Confirm how the minimum quantity is counted

Ask whether the minimum applies per fragrance, bottle size, packaging version or artwork design. A quantity spread across several versions may be treated differently from the same quantity of one confirmed item.

TopPerfume’s current route page lists selected logo and private-label options from 100 pieces. This is a starting point for eligible projects. Ask for the minimum quantity and available configuration for the exact product you are discussing.

Also ask what changes if you revise the bottle, fragrance, decoration or outer packaging. A finished-product wholesale minimum should not be used to budget a different custom project.

Review artwork and samples in separate steps

An artwork layout helps you review placement and text. A physical sample allows you to inspect the supplied materials and appearance. Ask which type of sample is available at each stage and what it represents.

Before approving the project, review:

  • The correct brand spelling, product wording and agreed artwork version.
  • Logo size, position and appearance on the selected component.
  • The bottle, cap and packaging configuration included in the quotation.
  • The selected fragrance sample or product reference, where applicable.
  • Any differences between the sample and the proposed bulk order.

Keep the approval record specific. Use a dated reference and an agreed list of components, rather than relying on a general “looks good” message. Ask for sample charges and shipping costs to be stated before proceeding.

Request a quotation with an agreed scope

Your quotation should identify the product, quantity, branding work and packaging included. Ask whether there are separate artwork, setup, sample or shipping charges, and which costs remain to be confirmed.

Discuss the timeline as stages: specification confirmation, artwork approval, sample review and dispatch planning. The applicable timing depends on the selected project. A general website dispatch indication should not become a fixed arrival promise for an unconfirmed custom order.

For repeat orders, ask how the approved specification will be referenced and whether availability, quantity requirements or pricing need to be reconfirmed.

Questions buyers often ask

Can I start by adding a logo without developing a new fragrance?

Ask about the existing options eligible for your own branding. Your logo brief can be reviewed separately from a new fragrance-development request; availability is confirmed by product and supplier.

Do I need finished artwork before contacting you?

You can start with a product direction, estimated quantity and preferred logo position. State whether your logo is ready and request the applicable artwork requirements before preparing the final layout.

Can I split the order across several designs?

Include the proposed quantity for each version in your brief. The minimum and setup arrangements must be checked for that configuration.

Does a catalogue product automatically support my own logo?

Customization eligibility is reviewed separately. Identify the product or format you like and ask which private-label options are suitable.

Discuss your custom logo perfume project

Send your product direction, logo placement, estimated quantity and destination through the TopPerfume contact page. If some details are undecided, include those questions in the brief.

You can also compare the existing wholesale and private-label routes before requesting a quotation. The aim of the first conversation is to identify a suitable product and a clear scope for the next decision.

seoTitle: Wholesale Perfume for a New Store: Guide | TopPerfume
description: Plan your first wholesale perfume order with a clear customer profile, sample shortlist, SKU quantities, cost comparison and supplier questions before you buy.
excerpt: Build a focused first fragrance order by matching products to your customers, comparing samples and confirming product-by-product buying terms.
title: Buying Wholesale Perfume for a New Store: Your First-Order Guide
html:
Your first perfume order shapes what customers see, what your team can explain and how much money is committed to stock. Before adding more products, give each item a clear reason to be in the assortment.

This guide helps new fragrance shops, beauty retailers and online sellers prepare a focused wholesale order. Start with your customers, build a shortlist, compare samples and confirm the terms for each product before committing to quantities.

Describe the customer you want to serve

Write a short buying brief for your store. Include who you expect to buy, how they will discover the products and the type of purchase you want to support.

For example, are you planning a gift-focused display, adding fragrance to an existing beauty shop or opening an online assortment with a few clearly differentiated choices? These are planning directions, rather than predictions of what will sell.

Record four starting points:

  • Your customers and sales channel.
  • The intended retail price range.
  • Product formats and sizes you want to consider.
  • The amount you can allocate to stock, samples and delivery.

When you discuss options with a supplier, this brief helps explain why one product may fit your plan better than another.

Give each shortlisted product a role

You can build a small assortment around distinct customer preferences or shopping occasions. Ask for the product information and samples needed to evaluate each choice.

A planning sheet might look like this:

Role in the assortment Candidate product Question to resolve before buying Planned quantity
An everyday fragrance option Add a product link Does the sample fit the customer preference you are targeting? Decide after review
A different scent direction Add a product link Is the difference clear enough to explain to a customer? Decide after review
A gift-focused option Add a product link Are the presentation, size and total cost suitable? Decide after review
A possible later addition Keep a reference What evidence would justify adding this product? Leave out of the first order if undecided

The rows are a planning example, not a fixed bundle or a recommendation to stock four specific products. Use only the roles that make sense for your business.

Browse the TopPerfume fragrance collection to identify actual product references. Where fragrance notes or other details are not listed, ask for the information rather than inferring it from the bottle colour or product name.

Compare samples before deciding the full quantity

For each sample, record the product name, size and the reference supplied. Keep scent preference separate from packaging observations so you can explain why you prefer one option.

You may want to compare:

  • Your impression of the fragrance and how it develops during your observation.
  • How you would describe it to your intended customers.
  • The spray, cap, bottle and packaging as received.
  • Whether the supplied product information answers your retail questions.

Use reasonably consistent conditions when comparing samples, and record the time and context of any longevity observations. Your own sample notes support a buying decision; they are not a substitute for substantiated product performance claims.

Ask the supplier to clarify any mismatch between the sample, the product description and the proposed bulk supply before proceeding.

Confirm buying terms product by product

A low minimum advertised for one item does not establish the minimum for an entire catalogue. Check the exact SKU and any variants you want to order.

For example, the Lattafa Khamrah 100 mL product page provides an individual product reference and its listed order terms. Use the current page and a written quotation for that item, then repeat the check for each additional product.

Ask these questions:

  1. What is the current minimum for this exact product or variant?
  2. Can my proposed order contain different products, and what minimum applies to each?
  3. Is the requested quantity available for the planned order?
  4. What packaging is included with the quoted item?
  5. What sample, dispatch and delivery arrangements apply?

If your plan includes your own logo, describe it as a separate project. TopPerfume’s wholesale and private-label routes have different starting points and require product-specific confirmation.

Compare the cost of getting the order to your business

Keep the product subtotal separate from the full purchasing cost. Use the actual quotation for your destination and scope.

Cost item What to record
Products Unit price multiplied by the agreed quantity for each item
Samples Any agreed sample and sample-shipping charges
Extra work Agreed branding, packaging or other project charges, if applicable
Freight and handling The quoted transport scope and any stated exclusions
Other applicable charges Amounts confirmed for your transaction and destination

Compare suppliers on the same product specification, quantities and included services. If an amount is unknown, keep it visible as an item to confirm rather than treating it as zero.

TopPerfume’s order information explains that listed product subtotals exclude shipping and taxes and that transaction arrangements are agreed for each order.

Plan how you will explain the products

A useful assortment gives you clear information to share with shoppers. Prepare a short product card for each selected item using confirmed details.

Include the name, size, product presentation and any verified fragrance information. Add your own sample observations where appropriate, clearly identified as observations. If a customer asks about a detail you have not confirmed, return to the supplier for the information.

For online selling, use product images that match what you will supply. For a physical display, consider how the packaging and product information will help customers compare the choices. This preparation also reveals gaps before you purchase the full assortment.

Keep a simple first-order and reorder record

After launch, track what customers ask about, what sells and what remains in stock. Separate sales from interest: a product receiving questions may still need better information, a different presentation or further sample review.

Before placing the first order, ask how to identify the same product for a repeat purchase, how availability is confirmed and what buying terms may change. Keep the supplier reference and agreed specification with your order record.

Use your early results to decide whether to reorder, adjust quantities or add another product. A new item should have a clear role in the assortment.

Questions new buyers often ask

How many perfume products should a new store start with?

There is no fixed count in this guide. Choose a number you can sample, explain and fund within your plan. The planning sheet helps you give each selected product a purpose.

Can I mix different perfumes in one order?

Send the proposed product list and quantity for each item. Mixed-order eligibility and minimum quantities need to be confirmed against those products.

Should I begin with wholesale products or my own brand?

Decide what your first launch requires. Finished-product wholesale and a private-label project involve different product choices, quantities and approvals. Compare the actual options against your customers, budget and timing.

What information should I send to get a useful quote?

Include your destination, product links, quantity per item, planned timing and any sample or customization request. Mention the questions you still need help resolving.

Prepare your first wholesale perfume enquiry

Choose your candidates from the fragrance collection, then contact TopPerfume with your first-order brief.

Information Your first-order brief
Store type and customers Describe your business and intended buyers
Destination Country and city
Product references Paste the selected product links
Quantities List units for each product or variant
Samples State what you want to review first
Branding Standard wholesale or a separate logo/custom project
Timing and open questions Add your preferred schedule and what needs clarification

TopPerfume supports wholesale beauty sourcing and supplier coordination. Sharing a focused brief makes it easier to review product options, confirm the applicable terms and prepare the next step for your order.

seoTitle: Compare Perfume Samples for Wholesale | TopPerfume
description: Compare perfume samples before a wholesale order. Record scent observations, spray and packaging checks, sample costs and questions in a practical buyer worksheet.
excerpt: Compare a fragrance shortlist with a blank observation worksheet, clear sample references and separate checks for scent, packaging and buying terms.
title: How to Compare Perfume Samples Before a Wholesale Order
html:
A perfume sample can help you decide what belongs in your shop, but a good first impression is only one part of the buying decision. You also need to know which product you received, how you compared it and which details still need a supplier's answer.

Use this guide to turn a shortlist into a recorded comparison. It is a retail buying worksheet, not a laboratory test or a promise about fragrance performance. Start with the products in your wholesale perfume shortlist, then keep observations separate from the facts supplied with each sample.

Identify every sample before comparing it

Give each sample a reference that you can use in notes, photographs and follow-up messages. Record the product name, supplier reference, date received and the size stated on the supplied label. If a batch or lot reference is present, copy it exactly; leave missing details unresolved.

Ask what the sample represents. A small fragrance vial may let you explore a scent, while a finished retail unit also lets you inspect its bottle, sprayer and carton. Neither should automatically be treated as approval of every component in a future order.

For example, the Lattafa Khamrah product page identifies a particular branded wholesale product. Ask about a sample of that exact reference and its current availability. It is not a proposal to put your logo on the branded product.

Before paying, confirm the sample reference, quantity, sample charge, shipping charge and destination. Sample availability can be confirmed for the selected product or project. Samples are charged, and shipping is paid by the buyer.

Separate scent preference from other buying criteria

Avoid reducing the entire decision to one score. A sample may match your shop's scent direction but have unresolved packaging details. Another may be well presented yet overlap too closely with a product you already sell.

Comparison area What to record What the note does not establish
Scent direction Your own description and the customer preference it might suit A verified ingredient list or an official scent-note specification
Perceived intensity How noticeable it seems under the conditions you record A universal projection or strength rating
Change over time Your observations at named times during the comparison A guaranteed wear duration for every customer
Spray and handling What you observe from the supplied sprayer, cap and bottle The condition of an entire future shipment
Packaging Visible condition, supplied components and label references Confirmation of uninspected packaging or a custom version
Commercial fit The questions about quantity, cost and replenishment that remain Current stock, an agreed bulk quote or a delivery commitment

Keep comparison conditions as consistent as practical

Choose a manageable group of samples and use a separate, clearly labelled fragrance blotter for each. Follow the supplied product instructions. Record how you applied each sample and keep the blotters separate so that your notes refer to the intended product.

Decide when you will revisit the samples and write down the actual observation times. Compare them in a similar setting, noting changes such as moving rooms or returning after a break. If the application method or surroundings differ, record the difference instead of presenting the observations as directly equivalent.

Describe what you notice in ordinary language. “Still noticeable on this blotter at this observation time” is more useful than a broad claim that the perfume lasts all day. If you also record personal wear observations from normal use, keep them separate from the blotter notes and identify the context. Neither record replaces product testing or supports a universal performance claim.

Keep individual feedback before discussing the result

If several buyers or colleagues compare the same shortlist, ask each person to record their impression before discussing a shared decision. Keep differing preferences visible. Your aim is to understand the assortment you want to buy, not to invent a unanimous test result.

Check the sample's physical presentation

Inspect the parcel and supplied components when they arrive. Photograph the item reference and any visible damage before separating the packaging. For a finished bottle, record the sprayer's observed operation, cap fit, visible leakage and the condition of the bottle and carton.

Send a specific question when something is unclear. “The sample arrived without an outer carton; is a carton included in the quoted retail unit?” gives the supplier something concrete to resolve. Do not silently assume that a sample's presentation is the final bulk specification.

Use a blank sample comparison record

Copy this table for each shortlisted product. Keep photographs and supplier replies under the same sample reference. Enter your own observations; the worksheet contains no preset grades or performance targets.

Record field Your entry
Sample reference and exact product To complete
Supplier reference and date received To complete
Labelled size; batch reference if present To complete
Sample format and components supplied To complete
Intended customer and assortment role To complete
Application method, setting and observation times To complete
Scent preference and changes observed To complete
Spray, cap, leakage and packaging observations To complete
Photo references and supplier questions To complete
Sample and freight charges quoted To complete
Decision: shortlist, revisit or decline To complete

Turn observations into a buying decision

Shortlist a sample when you can explain its place in your assortment and identify the remaining commercial questions. Revisit it when the sample reference, package contents or comparison conditions are unclear. Decline it when it does not fit the customer or presentation you are planning.

Before placing a wholesale order, link the selected sample to a written product specification and quote. Confirm the exact product, quantity, supplied packaging, price basis, current availability and dispatch arrangement. Do not treat sample approval as approval of a different size, fragrance or packaging version.

If you are still deciding the range and quantities, use the first wholesale perfume order guide alongside your sample notes.

Send a sample request that can be answered

Tell TopPerfume which products you want to compare, the number of samples requested, your destination and the questions that matter most to your buying decision. Include the expected wholesale quantity separately so that it is not confused with the sample quantity.

Ask for an itemized sample and freight quote before proceeding. TopPerfume coordinates sourcing and supplier discussions; the selected product and current terms need confirmation. You can include your completed worksheet when discussing order terms and your inquiry.

Questions buyers often ask

Does a sample prove how long a perfume will last?

Your record describes what you observed in the stated conditions. It does not prove a fixed wear duration for every person or setting. Ask for relevant product-specific evidence before using a performance claim in your own sales material.

Can I evaluate packaging from a fragrance vial?

A vial does not show the retail bottle, sprayer or carton unless those components are also supplied. Request the appropriate product presentation and confirm any differences before approving an order.

Does paying for a sample reserve wholesale stock?

Do not assume it does. Confirm stock allocation, the final order quantity and the applicable order terms separately with your quotation.

seoTitle: Lip Gloss or Eyeshadow? First Makeup Range | TopPerfume
description: Plan your first makeup collection: compare lip gloss and eyeshadow, organize shades, check sample details and separate wholesale terms from custom project MOQs.
excerpt: Choose a focused lip or eye range, record product and shade requirements, and separate finished-product buying from a custom branding project.
title: Lip Gloss or Eyeshadow? Planning Your First Makeup Collection
html:
Your first makeup collection needs a clear reason for customers to choose it. Start with the look they want, how they shop and the products you can explain well. Then decide whether a focused lip range, an eye palette or a carefully limited combination supports that plan.

This guide helps new brands and beauty retailers build a product and shade brief. It also separates two different requests: buying an existing finished product for resale and developing an eligible product under your own brand. A product in the TopPerfume makeup catalogue is a reference to discuss, not automatic confirmation of private-label eligibility.

Define the customer and the look before choosing products

Write a short description of your intended customer, sales channel and desired makeup finish. A store where customers can compare physical samples needs a different presentation plan from an online launch built around photographs and demonstrations.

Choose the role of each proposed product. It might introduce your colour direction, complement something you already sell or answer a specific request from your audience. Avoid adding shades simply to make the collection appear larger: each extra version creates another quantity, sample and specification to confirm.

Compare what lip gloss and eyeshadow need to show

Neither category is automatically the better first purchase. Compare the information you can obtain and the demonstration you can provide, as well as the appearance of the product itself.

Planning question Lip gloss or lip glaze Eyeshadow or an eye palette
What look are you offering? The selected colour direction, visible finish and coverage to evaluate The colour story, individual finishes and combinations to evaluate
What must a sample show? Appearance, observed texture, applicator and container Individual shades, application observations, pan layout and packaging
What needs a clear identity? Exact product, shade reference and version Exact palette and the shades included; whether it is sold as a fixed unit
What should customers see? Product and shade photographs under recorded conditions The full palette plus identifiable shade images and demonstrations
What remains a supplier question? Net content, ingredients, shade codes, quantities and customization eligibility Net weight, ingredients, shade identities, palette quantities and customization eligibility

The Hydrating Mirror-Shine Lip Glaze and Mocha Chocolate 9-Shade Eyeshadow Palette are two existing catalogue references you can use to start a discussion. The latter is presented as a nine-shade palette. Request the exact sample and available product information before selecting either for your range.

Names and catalogue images help identify the references. They do not establish wear duration, suitability for every skin tone, available custom shades or permission to apply your own logo.

Plan shades around a specific assortment

Describe the colour direction you want and how each proposed shade differs from the others. Use supplier shade codes when confirmed. Until then, mark a reference as provisional and connect it to a photograph or physical sample instead of inventing a code.

A screen image is useful for shortlisting, but it should not be your only colour record. Ask for samples and document the appearance under consistent lighting. Keep the product reference and the conditions attached to your photographs so that later decisions can refer to the same item.

Treat a palette and individual shades as different order units

A palette containing several shades may be supplied as one fixed product. That does not mean each pan can be selected, replaced or ordered separately. Ask whether you are quoting a finished palette, a selection from existing shade options or a separate development request.

For lip products, ask how the quantity is allocated between shades. Do not assume that a minimum for one reference can be divided across every colour shown in a catalogue.

Inspect the packaging before preparing your logo

Record the container, cap or closure, applicator or pan layout and any outer packaging supplied with the sample. Note the usable branding area as a question for the supplier; a visible surface is not proof that a particular printing method is available.

If you want your own brand, submit that as a separate project request. Ask which product options are eligible, what can change and which components the quote includes. Do not commission final artwork around an unconfirmed tube, palette or carton.

TopPerfume works as a trading and sourcing partner. Customization depends on the selected product, supplier and agreed scope. Perfume project minimums should not be transferred to a lip or eye product without confirmation of the applicable makeup project terms.

Ask exactly how the MOQ is counted

Request a written quantity breakdown covering the finished product, shade, packaging version and artwork version where relevant. Keep the finished-product wholesale requirement separate from logo or packaging customization requirements.

For example, an inquiry for several lip shades should list the proposed quantity of each shade, then ask whether the combination is accepted. It is a request for confirmation, not a claim that mixed shades satisfy a supplier's minimum.

Ask for product, customization, sample and freight costs to be identified separately. Sample availability can be confirmed for the selected product or project. Samples are charged, and shipping is paid by the buyer. No single sample charge or makeup customization minimum is assumed in this guide.

Record samples before making launch claims

Keep photographs of the product, shade identity, packaging and your application observations together. Follow the supplied usage instructions. Record the lighting, application method and any differences between comparisons instead of treating every photograph as directly equivalent.

Use observations to decide what to ask next. A preferred finish or texture is a selection note. It does not substantiate waterproof, fixed wear-time, ingredient, vegan or other claims that need product-specific evidence. Ask for the relevant information before putting such claims on packaging or a sales page.

Build a first-collection worksheet

Copy one row for each proposed product or version. Leave unresolved fields open until you have the corresponding sample or supplier response.

Planning field Your entry
Customer, market and sales channel To complete
Product type and role in the collection To complete
Product reference; confirmed shade or palette identity To complete
Desired look and sample observations To complete
Proposed quantity per product and shade To complete
Finished-product purchase or separate custom project To complete
Requested logo or packaging scope; eligibility response To complete
Net content, ingredients and other missing documents To complete
Sample charge and buyer-paid shipping quote To complete
Photo references, open questions and approval status To complete
Destination and preferred launch date To complete

Send a focused brief for the next step

Send your target customer, chosen product direction, shade plan, expected quantities and destination. State whether you want the existing finished product or need TopPerfume to review a separate private-label project. Attach product links so that similar-looking references are not confused.

Discuss timing after the product and customization scope are clear. Lead time depends on the customization scope and project requirements. A preferred launch date is a planning input, not a confirmed production or arrival commitment.

Use the contact and order-terms page to start that discussion with your worksheet and remaining questions.

Questions buyers often ask

Should I launch both lip and eye products at once?

Only include both when you can explain each product's role and confirm the samples, quantities and budget involved. A focused first range can be easier to describe and review; this is a planning choice, not a guaranteed sales outcome.

Can I put my logo on either catalogue reference?

Eligibility for these exact references needs confirmation. Ask for suitable project options and a specific quote. An existing product page or wholesale minimum does not establish customization availability.

Can different shades be combined to meet a minimum?

Submit the proposed breakdown and ask for the accepted allocation in writing. Mixed-shade or mixed-SKU rules must be confirmed for the product or project.

seoTitle: Perfume Packaging MOQ: Plan Your First Order | TopPerfume
description: Match perfume, logo, fragrance and packaging quantities before ordering. Review TopPerfume’s MOQ terms and use a practical quantity-planning checklist.
excerpt: Plan your first perfume order by matching finished quantities to bottles, branding, fragrance and packaging, with an illustrative example and a practical checklist.
title: Perfume Packaging MOQ: Match Component Quantities to Your First Order
html:
Suppose you want approximately 100 finished perfumes, while the custom packaging MOQ may be 300 pcs. This illustrative scenario is not a confirmed order or package offer. A higher packaging MOQ does not automatically mean you must order the same number of finished perfumes. First, confirm the packaging requirement's scope and counting basis, then ask how it applies to your finished-product target.

Before committing to a perfume project, connect your finished-product target to the fragrance, bottle, branding and packaging you want supplied. This guide explains how to record those quantities, spot a mismatch and ask the questions needed to resolve it before ordering.

TopPerfume Quick Answer — Current Customization Terms

Service MOQ
Private Label 100 pcs
Logo Customization 100 pcs
Custom Fragrance 100 pcs
Custom Packaging 300 pcs

These are TopPerfume's current customization terms, not universal industry standards. The applicable packaging scope and quantity allocation still need confirmation for your specific project.

Start with the finished order, then list its packaging components

Define units, sets and quantities per product version

Start with what you want delivered: the product, its presentation and the number of finished units. If you are planning several fragrances, sizes or designs, give each version its own reference and proposed quantity.

Be precise about the unit. A bottle, a carton and a gift set are different counting units. Ask what is included in one finished unit or set before using that figure to calculate component requirements.

Separate the bottle, closures, decoration and outer packaging

List the elements in your intended presentation. Depending on the project, these might include a bottle, sprayer, cap, label or bottle decoration, carton and insert. Keep the fragrance selection alongside that list so the packaging versions can be linked to the correct finished product.

A logo is work applied to an agreed item; it is not necessarily another physical component. Record where it will appear and which artwork version applies. This prevents a request for bottle branding from being mistaken for a request that also includes a printed carton.

Keep finished-product wholesale separate from a custom project

Buying an existing branded perfume and commissioning a product under your own brand are separate purchasing routes. A wholesale minimum for a catalogue product does not establish its eligibility for new branding or packaging.

Use the custom logo perfume buying guide if you still need to define your branding scope. If you want existing finished products, browse the wholesale fragrance collection and confirm the terms for each selected reference.

Why packaging components can have different MOQs

Existing components and new production do not have the same scope

A supplier may offer an existing bottle design, a decorated version of that design or a project requiring a new structure. These requests involve different work and may have different minimum order quantities.

An existing bottle design also does not establish the availability or quantity terms of a matching cap, sprayer or box. Confirm the complete proposed combination rather than treating the bottle listing as approval of the finished package.

Decoration, tooling and design changes may add separate minimums

Bottle decoration and carton printing may require their own artwork, setup and production arrangements. A new structure may introduce tooling requirements. A fragrance change may need a separate production scope from a change to the logo or carton.

These are reasons to ask for a breakdown, not grounds for assigning a standard minimum to every process. The applicable requirements depend on the supplier and the selected project.

Minimum being discussed What it may refer to What the buyer should clarify
Perfume product or private-label MOQ The agreed finished product or project configuration Which product, fragrance, size and presentation does it cover?
Bottle or closure MOQ A particular component specification Is the quantity tied to the model, size, colour or finish?
Logo customization MOQ Branding work on specified items Which surface, artwork and application scope are included?
Custom fragrance MOQ The selected fragrance customization scope How is the quantity counted if more than one fragrance is requested?
Custom packaging MOQ The agreed packaging specification and customization Which components and design versions does the stated minimum cover?

Ask what each minimum is counted against

A number is useful only when its scope is clear. Ask whether it applies per component, design, colour, size, fragrance or finished configuration. Also ask whether quantities must follow a stated pack or order increment.

Confirm the counting method and component requirements for your specific project before ordering.

Match component quantities to your first-order plan

Record the required quantity for each component and version

Begin with your proposed finished quantity, then identify what each finished unit requires. Use the agreed contents and units of measure to work out the component quantities. Keep separate rows for different specifications or artwork versions until the supplier confirms that they can be treated together.

This is why the perfume product MOQ alone is insufficient: meeting that minimum does not answer whether your chosen bottle presentation, branding and outer packaging can be supplied in the quantities requested.

Compare requirements with confirmed supplier quantities

Use a quantity-planning sheet like the one below. Repeat it for each finished-product version. Enter the finished target, specification references and date at the top; attach the supplier's written response to the same record.

Component or work scope Planned requirement Supplier-confirmed MOQ and counting basis Quoted quantity Open question or mismatch
Finished perfume and selected fragrance Units per fragrance/version To confirm To confirm Does the proposed allocation meet the applicable terms?
Bottle specification Units needed for the finished plan To confirm To confirm Is this exact bottle available for the requested scope?
Sprayer, cap and any other closures Record each component separately To confirm To confirm Are the selected parts and their quantities confirmed together?
Logo or decoration Items to be branded, by location and artwork To confirm To confirm Which items and versions does the branding quantity cover?
Carton, insert and any labels Record each component and design separately To confirm To confirm How does each required quantity compare with the proposed supply?

Replace “To confirm” only when you have an answer for that specification. Keep your requested quantity separate from the supplier's quoted quantity. An unanswered field is an open decision, not a zero or an accepted condition.

Flag mismatches without inventing a finished-order MOQ

If a component requirement exceeds your immediate needs, mark the difference for discussion. Do not add unrelated component minimums together to calculate a finished-product minimum. Equally, the highest number in the list does not automatically tell you how many finished perfumes you must purchase.

The next step is to confirm an arrangement covering the selected specifications, component purchases and finished delivery quantity.

Illustrative example: a 100-piece target and a 300-piece packaging requirement

Illustrative example only: the following numbers show a question a buyer may need to resolve. They do not describe an accepted TopPerfume order, a customer case or a fixed package offer.

Planning item Illustrative quantity What remains to be agreed
Finished perfume target 100 pcs Whether the selected product and complete presentation can be supplied for this target
Logo customization scope 100 pcs The branded item, artwork and applicable counting method
Custom packaging requirement 300 pcs Which packaging specification the quantity covers and how it relates to the finished order

The buyer should ask: “My target is 100 finished perfumes. What exactly does the 300-piece packaging requirement cover, and what quantities would I be purchasing and receiving?”

The figures alone do not determine whether the packaging is counted per design, whether anything can be shared across SKUs, or whether unused components can be retained for a future order. They also do not establish that the finished order must increase to 300 perfumes.

Confirm the counting method and component requirements for your specific project before ordering.

Review your options when quantities do not align

Ask about fewer versions or a different packaging specification

Tell the supplier which parts of the plan are essential and which are open to review. You might ask whether fewer artwork versions, a different presentation or an available component combination would make the requested quantity feasible.

These are questions to explore. A simpler appearance does not guarantee a lower MOQ, and an alternative is useful only once its specification, quantity and price have been confirmed.

Confirm whether shared components can be counted together

If several fragrances appear to use the same bottle or box, identify the proposed shared specification and list the quantity for each finished version. Ask whether the supplier accepts that allocation and whether different labels or artwork change the counting basis.

Similar-looking components do not establish permission to combine designs or SKUs. Obtain a written response identifying which specifications and quantities, if any, can be counted together.

Agree on any surplus-component arrangement before ordering

If the proposal involves purchasing more components than the first finished shipment will use, ask:

  • What additional quantity would be purchased, and at what cost?
  • Who would own those components, and when would they be delivered?
  • Is any storage arrangement offered, and what fees, duration and responsibilities would apply?
  • Could the components be used for a later order, and what specification or reorder conditions would need to be reconfirmed?
  • What happens if the artwork, bottle or product changes before they are used?

Record the agreed arrangement in writing. Do not build the order plan around assumed storage, future availability or automatic reuse.

Apply TopPerfume's project terms to the scope you requested

Distinguish private-label, logo, fragrance and packaging minimums

TopPerfume's current service-level conditions are:

Service Current TopPerfume MOQ
Private label 100 pcs
Logo customization 100 pcs
Custom fragrance 100 pcs
Custom packaging 300 pcs

These service figures do not establish a minimum for every individual packaging component or confirm the eligibility of every catalogue product.

Review TopPerfume's private-label and customization terms alongside the scope of your inquiry.

Confirm the packaging version and counting basis for your project

Identify the packaging you want, the design versions and your finished-product target. Ask how the applicable service conditions fit that exact request.

The figures above do not confirm that multiple designs or SKUs can share a 300-piece requirement. Nor do they establish a storage arrangement for unused packaging or require every product to be ordered as 300 finished units.

Confirm the counting method and component requirements for your specific project before ordering.

Keep samples and project timing separate from quantity approval

Sample availability can be confirmed for the selected product or project. Samples are charged, and shipping is paid by the buyer. Request the sample and freight amounts for your scope and destination.

Lead time depends on the customization scope and project requirements. Agreeing quantities does not, by itself, confirm a production schedule or arrival date.

Confirm the selected package before requesting a final quote

Match the component list to the relevant sample or specification

Check that the bottle, closures, branding and packaging references in your quantity sheet match the proposed supply. Ask which parts a sample represents and which still require confirmation. A fragrance sample alone does not approve a printed carton or a different bottle assembly.

For a fuller observation record, use the guide to comparing perfume samples before ordering.

Use this practical checklist before committing

  • Identify each finished product or fragrance version and its planned quantity.
  • Define what one finished unit or set includes.
  • List the required bottle, closures, decoration and packaging specifications.
  • Record each applicable MOQ, its counting basis and any order increments.
  • Separate requested quantities from quoted purchase and delivery quantities.
  • Obtain a written response for any proposed shared-component or mixed-design allocation.
  • Resolve quantity differences and any surplus-component responsibilities.
  • Link the agreed specifications to the relevant artwork, sample or approval reference.
  • Confirm sample charges, buyer-paid freight and project timing separately.
  • Keep the dated quantity breakdown with the quotation and remaining questions.

Send the version breakdown, open questions and destination

Send the completed plan with your destination and preferred launch timing. Highlight unresolved items so they can be addressed before you commit. If a specification changes, ask whether the affected quantities and terms need to be reconfirmed.

For broader assortment and cost planning, continue with the first wholesale perfume order guide.

Questions about packaging MOQ and first-order quantities

Why can perfume packaging MOQ be higher than the private-label MOQ?

The two minimums can refer to different work. A private-label minimum concerns the selected product configuration, while packaging may involve separate structures, printing, finishing or design versions. Ask which packaging specification and production requirements the higher quantity covers; it does not automatically set the finished perfume quantity.

Can I order 100 private-label perfumes if custom packaging MOQ is 300 pcs?

The two published minimums alone are not enough to confirm whether that order is feasible. Send your 100-piece finished-product target with the fragrance/version breakdown and packaging requirement. Ask TopPerfume to confirm the applicable counting basis, component purchase quantities and finished delivery quantity before you commit. Any treatment of packaging beyond the first order's needs requires a separate agreement.

Can different designs be combined to meet one packaging minimum?

Do not assume they can. List each design and proposed quantity, then ask the supplier to identify which allocations are accepted and which versions must meet a separate minimum.

Does a higher packaging MOQ automatically increase the finished perfume order?

The packaging figure alone does not establish the finished-order quantity. Ask the supplier to specify the component quantities you would purchase, the finished quantity you would receive and any conditions needed to make the proposal workable.

Can unused packaging be kept for a later order?

Only rely on that option if an arrangement has been explicitly agreed. Ownership, storage, costs, duration and future use all need clarification. TopPerfume's packaging MOQ does not by itself include such an arrangement.

Send your quantity plan for review

TopPerfume works as a trading and sourcing partner, coordinating project discussions with suppliers. Send your planned finished quantity, fragrance/version breakdown, packaging requirement and destination. Include packaging references and highlight any quantity mismatch or unanswered question so the requested scope is clear.

Send Your Quantity Plan for Review to discuss the applicable requirements before ordering.

title: How to Verify a Perfume Supplier Before Your First Order
description: Match supplier identity, product details, quotation scope and payment records before your first wholesale perfume order or private-label project.
excerpt: Match company, product, quotation and payment records before your first perfume order. Use practical checklists and follow-up questions to resolve missing or conflicting terms.
html:
You have received a perfume quotation, but the company name differs from the website’s trading name, the product description does not fully match your chosen SKU, or the payment recipient is another entity. These differences need an explanation before you accept or pay for the order. Match the company, product, quotation and payment records to establish who is supplying what, under which terms.

This guide provides a document-matching workflow for branded wholesale purchases and independent private-label projects. Verification helps you identify and resolve missing information; it is not certification of a supplier or a guarantee of an order’s outcome.

Quick Verification Summary

Check Core information to match or confirm
Supplier identity Connect the trading name, company, sales contact and quotation entity.
Business role Establish what the supplier does and who is responsible for the proposed supply.
Product / SKU Match the product or project reference, specification, version and buying route.
Quote scope Identify what the price includes, excludes and leaves unconfirmed.
Payment entity Explain the relationship between the seller, invoice entity and payment recipient.
Timing stage Distinguish production, dispatch, transit and delivery, including their starting conditions.

Verify who you are actually buying from

Start a record for the proposed order. Keep the supplier’s replies and documents together, using the same product or project reference throughout.

Connect the trading name, company and contact

Ask for the company name behind the trading name or website, its stated business address and registration jurisdiction, and the contact responsible for your inquiry. Where an appropriate public company register is available, use the supplied details to check that you are looking at the intended entity.

Compare that information with:

  • The company or trading name shown on the website.
  • The email address, domain and other contact channels being used.
  • The entity named on the quotation.
  • The proposed seller or invoicing entity.
  • The payment recipient identified for the order.

These names may describe different parts of a business arrangement. A trading name can differ from a company name; another entity may be involved in a transaction. Obtain and check the explanation rather than assume the difference is harmless or automatically dishonest.

Company information helps identify the business. Product authenticity, stock availability, brand relationships and the proposed supply require their own supporting information.

Identify what each document represents

Keep a dated copy of the quotation and note its version or reference. If you receive a revised quote, retain the earlier version and identify what changed.

A quotation describes a proposed supply. An invoice or order confirmation should be checked against the terms you accepted. Payment instructions identify where a payment is requested; a payment receipt records a payment.

If the documents use different names or references, ask which entity is selling to you and how the documents relate to the same order.

Clarify the supplier’s role in the perfume project

A supplier’s role should explain its responsibilities, not simply sound reassuring.

Claimed role What to clarify for your order
Brand owner Which brand is owned, and how does that relate to the products being offered?
Authorized distributor Which brand, territory or sales scope does the claimed authorization cover, and how can that relationship be checked?
Manufacturer Which production activities does the business actually perform, and which are handled elsewhere?
Trading company Which entity sells the goods, and who confirms sourcing, product information and order terms?
Sourcing partner What sourcing work is included, and who will be the seller and transaction contact?
Supplier coordinator Which parties or project stages are coordinated, and who answers questions about each part of the supply?

One business may perform more than one role. Different roles do not automatically mean better or worse supply. The question is whether the description matches the actual arrangement.

For a custom project, ask who will confirm the fragrance, bottle, decoration and packaging scope, and who will communicate changes. A general statement that a supplier “handles everything” leaves those responsibilities unclear.

TopPerfume works as a trading and sourcing partner, supporting supplier coordination. This does not describe TopPerfume as a manufacturer, factory owner or authorized distributor.

Separate a product listing from a brand relationship

A branded product listing does not prove authorization from the brand. If a supplier claims to be an authorized distributor or official partner, ask for information supporting that specific relationship, including its scope and how it can be checked.

Product images, invoices and batch references serve different purposes and should not be treated as automatic proof of authorization. Record whether the claimed relationship has been supported; an unanswered authorization question alone does not establish that the goods are counterfeit.

Match the product or project to the quote

Give every proposed order line an exact reference. Compare the product information you selected with the supplier’s quotation and any sample reference.

Check the product name, brand, SKU or supplier code, capacity, format, specification, version and quantity unit. If a supplier uses a different code from the website, ask it to confirm the correspondence in writing.

The wholesale fragrance collection provides product references for an inquiry. Confirm availability for your requested quantity separately.

Keep branded wholesale and private label separate

For branded wholesale, establish the exact finished product and packaging being offered. For a private-label project, establish the eligible product or configuration and the changes the supplier has accepted.

A low wholesale MOQ for an existing product does not mean that product can carry your logo. A website’s private-label service also does not establish that every branded SKU can be relabelled, repackaged or supplied with a different fragrance.

Ask separately:

  • Is this quotation for the existing branded product or an independent private-label project?
  • Which product or configuration is eligible for the requested customization?
  • Where will the logo appear, and which artwork version is being discussed?
  • What packaging and fragrance changes, if any, have been accepted?
  • What quantity requirement applies to that specific scope?

Use the custom logo perfume buying guide when you need to prepare the project itself. Supplier verification should then check that the quote refers to the brief you actually submitted.

Confirm what the MOQ applies to

TopPerfume’s current customization terms are:

Service Current MOQ
Private Label 100 pcs
Logo Customization 100 pcs
Custom Fragrance 100 pcs
Custom Packaging 300 pcs

These are TopPerfume’s current customization terms, not universal industry standards. Product eligibility, project scope and the applicable counting basis still require confirmation.

They do not establish that every packaging component has the same minimum, that multiple SKUs can share a minimum, or that a branded wholesale product is eligible for customization.

Review the wholesale and private-label routes for the service context. If component quantities differ from your finished-order target, use the packaging quantity-planning guide rather than inventing a new finished-product MOQ.

Check what the quotation actually includes

Check one quotation against your intended order before comparing it with another offer. A unit price is difficult to interpret when the product, packaging or customization scope is incomplete.

For each scope item, record Included, Not included or Still to confirm, together with the supplier’s supporting reference. A blank field is not a zero charge or an agreement.

Quote Verification Table

Field Details to match or record Question if the quote is incomplete
Product / SKU Exact product, brand, capacity, specification and version “Which product reference does this line supply?”
Quantity Units per SKU or version, order unit and applicable MOQ “Is this quantity counted per product, fragrance, design or another basis?”
Unit price Currency, price per stated unit, quantity basis and subtotal “Which specification and quantity does this price cover?”
Logo Branded item, position, artwork reference and agreed work “Is this branding included, separately charged or still awaiting confirmation?”
Packaging Bottle, sprayer, cap, label, carton and other requested components “Which components are supplied, and which are excluded or unquoted?”
Fragrance customization Accepted scent scope and its project reference “Does the quote include this fragrance request, or only the existing option?”
Sample Availability, sample type, quantity, sample charge and shipping charge “What will the sample represent, and what will it cost?”
Other project work Any applicable artwork, setup, tooling or other requested work “Are there additional charges for this scope?”
Freight Destination, payer, quoted transport scope and exclusions “What does the freight amount cover, and what remains outside it?”
Other charges Any applicable taxes, handling or transaction-specific amounts “Which amounts are confirmed, excluded or still unknown?”
Dispatch / production timing Relevant stage, starting condition and estimated timing “Does this refer to production, dispatch or arrival?”
Quote version and terms Date, reference, validity and linked written conditions “Which version and terms will the order use?”

For a bundled price, ask the supplier to describe what the bundle includes. You do not need to invent a price for every component, but you do need to know the agreed supply.

Request explicit confirmation of exclusions too. “Packaging included” is less useful than an identified bottle-and-carton configuration. “Custom fragrance” does not automatically establish formula ownership or exclusivity.

Broader assortment planning and comparison of purchasing costs belong in the first wholesale perfume order guide. Here, the task is to establish what this particular quotation means.

Separate samples, dispatch, production and delivery

These terms answer different questions and should have separate entries in your order record.

Confirm the sample’s scope and charges

For TopPerfume, sample availability can be confirmed for the selected product or project. Samples are charged, and shipping is paid by the buyer.

Ask for the actual sample and shipping amounts for your request. Do not assume a sample charge will be credited against a later order unless that arrangement is expressly confirmed.

Record whether the sample represents the fragrance alone, a finished retail product or an agreed custom configuration. A sample does not confirm the full bulk order: identify the components and versions it covers, along with any differences still requiring approval. Paying for a sample also does not automatically reserve wholesale stock.

For observation and comparison methods, use the perfume sample comparison guide.

Record the timeline by stage

Stage What your record should establish
Production lead time The work required and the conditions from which its timing starts
Dispatch When the prepared order is expected to leave the supplier
Shipping / transit time The transport estimate for the agreed route and service
Arrival / delivery The expected destination milestone and any conditions affecting it

TopPerfume’s current stock-order wording is:

For in-stock orders, dispatch is typically around 7 days after order confirmation.

This applies to dispatch of confirmed in-stock orders. It is not a seven-day delivery or private-label production commitment.

For independent private-label and custom projects:

Lead time depends on the customization scope and project requirements.

Ask what “order confirmation” means for your proposed transaction and which decisions remain outstanding. Buyer-paid freight does not, by itself, define the shipping service, customs arrangements, taxes or other delivery responsibilities.

Verify payment and transaction records before paying

Compare the payment recipient, seller and invoice entity with the commercial documents. If the names differ, ask how they are related and which entity is responsible for the sale. Matching names do not guarantee safety; unexplained differences require clarification.

If payment instructions change suddenly, reconfirm them through a previously verified or independently obtained company contact channel—not only by replying to the message announcing the change. This follows the FBI’s guidance on business email compromise.

Keep the dated quotation, invoice or order confirmation, agreed written terms and verified payment instructions under the same order reference. Add the payment receipt when applicable; dispatch and delivery need separate records.

TopPerfume’s payment methods and transaction conditions are negotiated for each order and confirmed in writing. Submitting a website inquiry does not create an order.

What to do when information does not match

Do not resolve a difference by choosing whichever document seems more convenient. Identify the conflicting fields, ask a precise question and request a clear record of the answer.

Use this sequence:

  1. Name the difference. Identify both documents or messages, their dates and the fields that disagree.
  2. Ask what each reference means. The difference may concern identity, scope, version or timing.
  3. Request the applicable terms in writing. Ask which entity, product, quantity or condition will apply to your order.
  4. Obtain a correction where necessary. A revised quote should identify the accepted scope and any resulting changes.
  5. Recheck affected fields. A packaging or fragrance change may require quantity, price, sample and timing confirmation again.
  6. Keep unresolved items open. Pause the affected approval or payment step if you cannot establish what you would be accepting.

Turn a mismatch into an answerable question

Information that does not match Specific question to send What to record before proceeding
Website and quotation use different company names “Why is the company name different? Which entity will sell to us, and how does it relate to the website’s trading name?” The explained relationship and the entity identified for the transaction
Payment recipient differs from the quotation or invoice “Who is the selling or contracting entity, who receives the payment, and what is their relationship?” The explanation and independently reconfirmed payment instructions
Product listing is branded wholesale, but a message offers your logo “Is this the existing wholesale SKU or a separate product eligible for customization? Which reference will the quotation cover?” An identified product or project and its accepted customization scope
MOQ differs between the page and quote “What exactly does each minimum apply to, and which requirement applies to my proposed SKU or project version?” The applicable quantity, unit and counting basis
A chat message mentions a box that the quote does not identify “What packaging is included in the quoted price? Please identify anything excluded or awaiting quotation.” A component description linked to the current quote
A sample differs from the quoted size or presentation “Which parts of the proposed order does this sample represent, and which differences still need approval?” The sample reference, differences and required follow-up
“Seven days” appears without a defined stage “Does this refer to dispatch of confirmed stock, production or transport? What starts the timing?” The relevant stage, starting condition and qualified estimate
Terms remain scattered across messages “Which terms are still subject to confirmation, and can the agreed points be linked to this quotation version?” One current record of accepted and unresolved points

Illustrative example: a wholesale quote and a logo request

Illustrative example only—not a TopPerfume order, customer case or confirmed service offer.

A buyer receives a quotation for a branded wholesale perfume. Later, a message says a logo request can be discussed, but the quote still identifies the original branded product and contains no branding scope.

The buyer should not interpret that message as approval to customize the quoted SKU.

The next question is: “Does the logo discussion concern this exact product or a separate private-label option? Please identify the eligible product and the branding scope before revising the quote.”

If a separate option is proposed, it needs its own confirmed reference, quantity, price, packaging, sample scope and timing. If eligibility remains unanswered, the logo requirement stays unresolved. The original wholesale quotation has not become a private-label agreement.

This is the value of matching records: it exposes the missing decision without inventing the answer.

Keep a short unresolved-item record

Field in question Conflicting references and dates Question sent Supplier reply / supporting reference Outcome
Enter the exact field Identify both sources State what needs explaining Link the dated answer or revised document Record matched, request more information, or pause the decision

Mark a field “matched” only for the identified scope and supporting reference. If that scope changes, reopen the affected check.

First-order perfume supplier verification checklist

Before accepting the proposed order, check that you can locate the relevant information—not simply recall a reassuring conversation.

  • Company identity: The trading name and company information are identified, with unexplained differences resolved.
  • Business role: The supplier’s stated role and responsibilities match the proposed transaction.
  • Product / SKU: Product references, capacity, specification, version and order units correspond across the records.
  • Brand relationship: Any claimed authorization or official relationship has been addressed separately from the product listing.
  • MOQ: The applicable minimum and counting basis are recorded for the selected product or project.
  • Customization eligibility: Logo, packaging and fragrance requests have specific answers; branded wholesale eligibility has not been assumed.
  • Sample: Availability, supplied scope, charges and the relationship to the proposed order are clear.
  • Packaging: Included components and any differences from the sample are identified.
  • Quote scope: Included, excluded and unconfirmed items are visible in the current quotation record.
  • Freight: The payer, destination, transport scope and outstanding charges or responsibilities are identified.
  • Dispatch / lead time: Production, dispatch, transit and delivery have not been confused.
  • Payment entity: The recipient and instructions correspond to the explained transaction arrangement; unexplained changes have been reconfirmed.
  • Written confirmation: The current quote, agreed terms, revisions and unresolved questions are retained together.

Keep unanswered items visible and assign each a follow-up question before treating the review as complete.

Frequently asked questions

How can I check whether a perfume supplier is legitimate?

Identify the company, its contact channels and its role in the proposed supply. Then match the exact product or project to the quotation, written terms and payment recipient. Check specific claims using relevant supporting information and follow up on inconsistencies.

The result is a documented basis for your decision, not a universal legitimacy certificate.

Does a low MOQ prove a supplier can offer private label?

No. A wholesale minimum may apply only to an existing finished product. Private-label eligibility, logo work, packaging and fragrance scope require separate confirmation for the proposed project.

What should be included in a perfume supplier quotation?

It should identify the supplier, quotation version, product or project, specifications, quantities, units, price and currency. The included supply, exclusions, outstanding charges, applicable timing and written transaction conditions should also be clear.

Where samples, customization or freight are involved, record their scope and charges explicitly.

Should the payment company name match the quotation or invoice?

Compare the names and establish the relationship between the seller, invoicing entity and payment recipient. If they differ, obtain a specific explanation and verify the instructions through an independently checked contact channel before paying.

What should I do if supplier information does not match?

Identify the conflicting fields and their source documents. Ask which information applies to your order, request a corrected or clearly linked written record, and recheck any affected quantity, price, scope or timing.

If a material difference remains unresolved, pause the related approval or payment decision.

Does a sample confirm the bulk order?

Only the identified sample and the parts it represents have been available for your review. Link its reference to the proposed specification and record any differences, components or order conditions that still need confirmation.

Send Your Product & Quote Details for Review

TopPerfume works as a trading and sourcing partner. To discuss the supply you are considering, send:

  • The product name, SKU or product link.
  • Your intended quantity, with a breakdown by product or version.
  • Whether you need wholesale supply or an independent private-label project.
  • Any logo, packaging or fragrance customization requirements.
  • Your TopPerfume quotation reference, if available, and the fields or terms you want clarified.
  • The destination country and city.

Highlight anything that does not match between your request, the product information and the quotation. This gives the discussion a specific starting point and keeps outstanding questions attached to the correct product or project.

Send Your Product & Quote Details for Review to clarify the requested supply and applicable terms before ordering.
